name: Double Draw Dominoes
description: Double Draw is a domino line game using a double-six set. Each turn a player must play two tiles at a time, one on each end of the line, matching by suit. If unable to play, the player draws one tile from the boneyard (when not empty) and passes. The round ends when someone empties their hand (dominoes), when the game is blocked, or when everyone has passed. Lowest pip count in hand wins the round; game is played to 100 points (two-player or partnership) or 61 points (three or four players).

history.origins: Variant of the standard draw domino game; documented in published rule references (Joe Celko, 2001). Requires playing two tiles at a time, one on each end of the line.
timeline: 2001: Documented in published rule references (Joe Celko).
history.cultural: Part of Western domino line games; often played with cribbage board for scoring (100 or 61 points).
history.evolution: Evolved from standard draw domino with the added constraint of playing in pairs on both ends.

setup.players: 2 to 4 players. Best for two to four.
setup.dealing: One player is dealer. Each player receives (8 minus the number of players) tiles. The dealer draws one tile at random from the remainder and turns it face up to start the line. Remaining tiles form the boneyard face down.

rules.objective: Win rounds by emptying your hand (domino) or having the lowest pip count when the game is blocked. First to reach the target score (100 in two-player or partnership, 61 in three or four-handed) wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Tiles are laid end to end matching suits. Player to dealer's left leads. Each turn: play two tiles (one on each end of the line), or if unable and boneyard not empty draw one tile and pass, or if boneyard empty and one tile left play that tile on either end, or if boneyard empty and cannot play then pass. Anyone may call blocked game; hands are then scored. Round ends when someone dominoes, blocked game is called, or everyone has passed.
keyRules: Play exactly two tiles per turn (one on each end of the line), except when boneyard is empty and you have only one tile.
If you cannot play and boneyard is not empty, draw one tile and pass.
Lowest pip total in hand at round end wins the round; winner receives sum of losers' totals minus own total. Tie for lowest: no score.
Game to 100 points (two-player or partnership) or 61 points (three or four-handed).

strategy.basic: Prioritize playing two tiles that keep both ends of the line flexible; avoid leaving a single suit dominant on one end.
strategy.intermediate: Count suits; know which pip values are likely unavailable on the ends. If the lead was 3-4, 3 and 4 may be scarce. Decide when to call blocked game to maximize opponent penalty.
strategy.advanced: Strategize so both ends change each play; use suit counting to force blocks when it benefits you. Call blocked game to keep scores lower when advantageous.
tips: Both ends change on each successful play, so planning ahead is hard; focus on which suits will not be on the ends.
Calling blocked game stops play and scores hands; use it to limit how high scores get.

variations.name: Partnership
variations.description: Four players in two partnerships; partners sit opposite. Same rules; game to 100 points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Partnership changes only seating and scoring side; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: 61 points (three or four-handed)
variations.description: When playing three or four-handed (non-partnership), game is played to 61 points so a cribbage board can be used for scoring.

scoring.description: At round end each player totals pips in hand. Lowest total wins the round and is credited with (sum of losers' totals minus own total). Tie for lowest: no score. Game is played to 100 points (two-player or partnership) or 61 points (three or four-handed); first to reach target wins.
scoring.winCondition: Win rounds by dominoing (empty hand) or having lowest pip count when blocked or all pass. First to reach target score (100 or 61) wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: Double Draw: domino line game for 2–4 players. Play two tiles per turn (one per end); draw from boneyard when unable to play. Lowest pip count wins round; first to 100 or 61 points wins.
